transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-09-09
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood CSM), Sofia (Argentis Head ML Infra), Jacob (CTO), Neha (Sec & Compliance), Marco (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick renewal check-in to confirm Argentis' preferred capacity uplift, add two new regions for production (eu-west + ap-southeast), and align on contract term and technical onboarding steps. Main asks: predictable burst capacity, KMS integration for private keys, and a short benchmark to validate latency/cost tradeoffs. Redwood will provide trial geocluster and revised SOW with tiered pricing options.

Topics Covered:
- Current usage patterns and projected Q4 ramp
- Dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs and cost modeling
- Geocluster provisioning timeline and failover policy
- Security (KMS, audit logs, SOC2, data residency)
- Benchmarks: latency SLA and cost-per-token expectations
- Next steps and SOW/contract options

Action items recap included above.

Transcript Body:
00:00 Ethan: Okay everyone uh good afternoon — thanks for joining. quick roll call?
00:08 Sofia: Heyhi this is Sofia, we are on, Jacob here too.
00:11 Jacob: Yep hi.
00:12 Ethan: Great. Priya and Liam from our side also on. Priya do you want to run the technical agenda quick?
00:20 Priya: Sure. We'll cover what Argentis is asking for — two region additions (eu-west and ap-southeast), planned capacity bump of ~2.5x for peak batch jobs, and how Redwood can provision a geocluster trial and what telemetry we'll include. Then discuss KMS/HSM and compliance questions.
00:41 Sofia: That sounds right. To be clear — we want predictable cold-start latencies for customers in EU and APAC; currently we're seeing 350-500ms p95 from our single-region setup and that's not good enough.
00:54 Priya: Understood. For p95 we typically recommend dedicated pools with warm warm-keep and aggressive prefix caching; there is a tradeoff of cost, obviously. we can show two profiles in the SOW: a latency-optimized and a cost-optimized profile.
01:10 Jacob: And what about burst? we have occasional spikes during nightly batch scoring, could we get burst capacity without overcommitting?
01:18 Ethan: Yes, burst is a standard pattern. We can reserve baseline capacity and allow reserved plus burst — billing for burst as usage overage or via a burst credit pool. We'll outline that in the SOW.
01:29 Marco: question — will geocluster mean active-active routing or active-passive failover? how does traffic split and consistency of KV cache look?
01:37 Priya: Good q. For the trial we'll provision active-active with smart routing by region (latency preference) and sticky KV caches per region. Cross-region KV sync is eventual, so for very low-latency customer-facing requests we keep KV local and fall back to prefix caching to reduce cold starts.
01:56 Neha: on security: we need to validate KMS integration and ensure that keys never leave our control. We also need to see retention windows for audit logs — 7 years for some regulated pods.
02:08 Priya: We support customer-managed KMS (Cloud KMS/HSM) in Private and Dedicated with key policies; we'll share the integration checklist. Audit logs can be pushed to your SIEM and retention enforced on your side — we can offer retention assistance for hosted customers as an add-on.
02:28 Neha: If we go hosted, are you able to provide an SOC2 attestation with a carve-out for customer-managed keys? also will you provide per-request logs with request IDs?
02:38 Liam: yes we publish SOC2 Type II; for hosted we'll include audit logs and request traces; per-request IDs are available and can be correlated to your shipper. We'll note any carve-outs in the security pack we share.
02:53 Sofia: Good. On the timeline — we want to be live in EU by mid October and APAC by end of October if possible. Is that realistic?
03:02 Ethan: That's tight but feasible if we get the SOW signed by next week and your security team thumbs up on KMS checklist quickly. Priya, is the infra provisioning timeline for two regions under three weeks?
03:12 Priya: For a geocluster trial yes — 5-7 business days to stand up the trial with telemetry. Full production-grade Dedicated pools with autoscaling and SLA onboarding is usually 3-4 weeks depending on quotas and network peering.
03:26 Marco: network peering — we need VPC peering and our egress policies — how do you handle that for Private vs Dedicated?
03:33 Priya: Dedicated: we can do VPC peering and private endpoints. Private deployments give you full control with our control plane, and on-prem we hand over an appliance. Hosted: TLS in transit + customer VPC endpoints for data plane are possible in certain regions. We'll include exact network diagrams.
03:52 Jacob: Cost modeling — can you give a quick sketch of expected delta between latency-profiled dedicated pools and cost-optimized shared-hosted?
04:01 Ethan: Yes. Rough ballpark for Argentis workload: latency-profile dedicated pools ~1.6x cost vs shared-hosted but p95 latency improves by ~30-40%. Cost-optimized dedicated with quantization/packing + caching can be within ~1.1x of hosted for many workloads. We'll attach a worked example.
04:24 Sofia: Important for us — if we do a 24-month commitment, what are the terms for capacity changes? we don't want to be locked if we undershoot or exceed.
04:33 Ethan: We typically offer quarterly adjustment windows and a two-way true-up: if you exceed committed units we bill delta at agreed overage rates; if you underutilize we allow a one-time realignment each 12 months. More flexible terms can be negotiated for longer commitments.
04:52 Neha: auditing question: do you provide immutable logs for model inferences (not PII but index IDs) for compliance?
04:59 Priya: We can provide per-request metadata logs with non-sensitive identifiers and hash pointers. For PII we recommend token scrubbing on your side before ingestion.
05:12 Marco: For the geocluster trial — what metrics will you expose? we'd like token-cost breakdown, GPU-utilization, p95/p99 latencies, and cold-start counts.
05:21 Priya: We'll include those plus KV-hit ratios and batching stats. We'll also enable a cost-simulator so you can see projected monthly cost based on your histogram.
05:33 Sofia: Great. Also, we had a quick concern — DeepServe approached us with a lower list price if we go multi-year. Any thoughts on how Redwood differentiates?
05:42 Ethan: We'll emphasize production observability, predictable unit economics, and our geocluster routing and KV cache optimizations. We can show past benchmark readouts with similar customers. Also, our failover policies and SLO-backed runbooks are differentiators.
06:00 Jacob: ok. Regarding benchmarks — what harness do you need from us? we can give a replay log of typical traffic and a synthetic workload.
06:08 Priya: The replay logs are perfect; ideally a 48-hour representative window plus a synthetic spike script. We'll run night-batch and peak interactive tests. Liam will coordinate specific metrics to capture.
06:20 Liam: I'll send the benchmark template after the call. We'll ask for endpoints, auth creds for test, and a 48-hour sample set.
06:26 Neha: encryption at rest — do you encrypt model artifacts and KV?
06:30 Priya: Yes encryption at rest with customer-managed keys for Dedicated/Private; hosted uses provider-managed keys by default unless you bring your own KMS.
06:39 Sofia: If we go ahead with the trial, can we get a brief runbook for failover — e.g., what to expect when region fallback occurs?
06:46 Priya: We'll supply a documentation pack and run a tabletop drill during the trial. For active-active we do region-preference routing and TTL-based fallback to secondary region if needed; we'll outline error modes and estimated latency impacts in the runbook.
07:05 Jacob: Sounds good. Any blockers on your side to get the SOW moving?
07:09 Ethan: The only things we need ASAP are signed MSA amendment for capacity trial, confirmation on KMS approach, and a primary contact for provisioning.
07:18 Sofia: I'll be that contact, Neha will handle security signoffs.
07:21 Ethan: Great. We'll get the SOW and two pricing tiers over by Monday.
07:25 Sofia: Perfect. thanks all.
07:28 Ethan: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the SOW and trial access details, and schedule the benchmark for the week of Sep 20.
07:35 (meeting ends)
